Thinking it through as myself...

I've farmed this land since my twenties. My family has about 10 mu here in Quzhou. The land is flat, the groundwater is there but we've been warned it's going down every year. I don't have money to gamble on new things — I need stable income to cover my son's tuition.

The only real choice here is what everyone does: **winter wheat followed by summer maize**. The whole village does this rotation. The grain station buys both. I know these crops. My father grew them.

For wheat, I'll plant Kenong 199 — it's reliable in this county, the ag station has been pushing it for years and my neighbor got good yields last autumn. I'll do rotary tillage in October before seeding, put down compound fertilizer at planting, then top-dress urea at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: the winter water in November to protect roots, then jointing, then heading. Maybe I cut one irrigation compared to what I used to do — my son read something about the aquifer dropping and it worried me.

For maize, I'll direct seed Zhengdan 958 right after wheat harvest in June — no time to till, and the moisture stays better that way. Summer rains usually handle most of the water need. I'll only pump once if July is dry. Maize gets less fertilizer attention from me; the residual from wheat helps.

Two pesticide sprays per crop — one early, one at key disease risk. I'm not doing more because the cost adds up and I watch the crop carefully.
